soul_reaver.name: Soul Reaver
soul_reaver.lore: Few who have held the Soul Reaver remember doing so willingly. The blade selects its wielders, and the criteria are opaque. What is known: wounds it inflicts do not heal without magic; the blade whispers between kills; and it grows heavier if used against the innocent. Its origin is attributed variously to a dying god, a betrayed archmage, and a particularly vengeful plague.

dawnbreaker.name: Dawnbreaker
dawnbreaker.lore: Dawnbreaker is the hammer that ended the First Darkness, when the elder dead walked the surface and the sun was a rumour. The head holds a sliver of preserved dawn, sealed in adamantine by a smith whose name was burned out of every chronicle the priests could find. Undead creatures struck by it take triple damage from the light: their flesh remembers what it was supposed to be afraid of, and obeys. The faint gold gleam at the hammer's seam never quite goes out, even in a closed sack.

venomfang.name: Venomfang
venomfang.lore: A master poisoner's commission from an earlier age. The spikes of Venomfang are hollow, filled with a venom that was synthesized from the distilled suffering of a hundred different creatures. The weapon weeps a thin dark ichor when hungry, which is often. The bleed it inflicts does not merely cut — it corrupts.

excalibur.name: Excalibur
excalibur.lore: The sword in the stone was not merely a test of strength but of worthiness — a distinction Arthur understood only after he had already proven himself in other ways. The blade predates its legend; Merlin admitted he found it. An inscription along the fuller reads in a language older than Latin: 'Take me up; cast me away.' Most kings have trouble with the second part.

durendal.name: Durendal
durendal.lore: Roland's sword contained within its golden hilt a tooth of Saint Peter, blood of Saint Basil, hair of Saint Denis, and a fragment of the Virgin's raiment. At Roncevaux, rather than let it fall to the Saracens, Roland struck it three times against a stone. The stone split each time. Durendal did not.

gram.name: Gram
gram.unidentified_name: a shining foreign blade of pale steel
gram.lore: Odin thrust Gram into the Branstock oak; only Sigmund drew it. His son Sigurd had the pieces reforged and with Gram slew Fafnir the dragon, tasted its blood, and thereafter understood the speech of birds. Its edge cuts through any armor, any hide, any enchantment — nothing can resist it.

broken_gram.name: Broken Blade of Gram
broken_gram.unidentified_name: a broken sword hilt with a jagged blade
broken_gram.lore: The shattered remains of a legendary blade. Odin himself broke it against Sigmund's shield when the hero's time had come. The hilt is wrapped in cracked leather and the blade ends in a jagged fracture halfway up. It is a poor weapon — but something about it still hums with dormant power.

sigurds_shovel.name: Sigurd's Shovel
sigurds_shovel.lore: It's just an ordinary shovel. Really. Not everything has to be a magic sword. Sigurd dug a pit with one of these and stabbed a dragon in the belly from below — sometimes the right tool is the humble one.

tyrfing.name: Tyrfing
tyrfing.unidentified_name: a sword that vibrates with cold malice
tyrfing.lore: The dwarves Dvalinn and Durin forged Tyrfing under duress and cursed it: it would kill a man every time unsheathed. The blade never rusts, never dulls, cuts through iron and stone. Three kings of the Hervarar line died by it. The curse is intrinsic to those who lack the wisdom to set it down.

fragarach.name: Fragarach
fragarach.unidentified_name: a slender blade with a sea-blue shimmer
fragarach.lore: The Answerer. No armour could stop it; no man could move once it was held to his throat. Manannan mac Lir forged it; Lugh carried it to end Fomorian tyranny. The Irish poets called it the Wind from the East.

caladbolg.name: Caladbolg
caladbolg.unidentified_name: a massive greatsword of unearthly make
caladbolg.lore: Fergus mac Róich's great sword could cut the tops off three hills with one sweep. Forged in the Otherworld, it has no human metallurgical analogue. The original has no fragments because it has never broken.

joyeuse.name: Joyeuse
joyeuse.unidentified_name: a radiant blade that shifts colour in lamplight
joyeuse.lore: Charlemagne's coronation sword changed colour thirty times per day and shone so brightly that enemies were dazzled before the first blow. Charlemagne was buried with it at Aachen. Or possibly wasn't. The trail goes cold in the ninth century.

hrunting.name: Hrunting
hrunting.unidentified_name: an ancient iron-dark blade etched with serpents
hrunting.lore: Unferth lent Hrunting to Beowulf for his descent into the mere. The poem calls it hardened in the blood of battle and says it had never failed any man who grasped it. In the underwater fight with Grendel's mother, it failed once. That was its single exception.
hrunting._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=52, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(52) x 1.65), min_level=40, quiz_tier=3.

skofnung.name: Skofnung
skofnung.unidentified_name: a cold grey blade with a dim inner glow
skofnung.lore: Taken from King Hrólf Kraki's burial mound; the twelve berserkers who served him in life inhabited the blade. Wounds dealt by Skofnung could only be healed by the Skofnung Stone. No healer has replicated the Stone.

gungnir.name: Gungnir
gungnir.unidentified_name: a perfectly balanced spear of dark ash
gungnir.lore: An oath sworn on Gungnir's tip is unbreakable. Odin threw it over the Vanir's heads to begin the first war. It has never missed. At Ragnarok he will throw it at the Fenris Wolf. This will not be a contradiction.
gungnir._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=91, base=37 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(91) x 1.65).

gae_bulg.name: Gáe Bulg
gae_bulg.unidentified_name: a barbed spear of sea-monster bone
gae_bulg.lore: Made from the bone of the Coinchenn sea-beast, thrown with the foot. When it entered a body it opened thirty barbs — it could not be withdrawn. Cu Chulainn used it twice in single combat; both times he wept after.

spear_of_longinus.name: Spear of Longinus
spear_of_longinus.unidentified_name: a Roman pilum with a blackened tip
spear_of_longinus.lore: Longinus pierced Christ's side at the crucifixion. Blood and water ran from the wound; Longinus was healed of failing eyesight. Charlemagne carried it in 47 battles. He died the one day he set it down.

mjolnir.name: Mjolnir
mjolnir.unidentified_name: a short-handled hammer of unsettling weight
mjolnir.lore: The handle came out short due to Loki's sabotage, but Odin declared it the greatest treasure ever made. Thor wore iron gauntlets to wield it. At Ragnarok he will kill the Midgard Serpent, take nine steps, and fall. The hammer will survive him.
mjolnir._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=92, base=42 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(92) x 1.75).

sharur.name: Sharur
sharur.unidentified_name: a golden mace that hums faintly
sharur.lore: The 'Smasher of Thousands,' weapon of Ninurta, the Sumerian god of war and agriculture. Sharur could fly through the air and speak — it served as Ninurta's scout, reporting enemy positions before battle. Its strikes scramble the minds of those it hits, leaving them confused and directionless.
sharur._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=45, base=10 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(45) x 1.55), min_level=37, quiz_tier=3.

ruyi_jingu_bang.name: Ruyi Jingu Bang
ruyi_jingu_bang.unidentified_name: a massive iron pillar banded with gold
ruyi_jingu_bang.lore: The Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod, originally a pillar used by Yu the Great to measure the depth of the world-flood. It weighs 17,550 pounds and can grow to fill the space between heaven and earth or shrink to the size of a needle. Sun Wukong stole it from the Dragon King's palace. Its reach is unmatched — enemies three paces away are within striking distance.
ruyi_jingu_bang._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=82, base=30 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(82) x 1.7), min_level=70, quiz_tier=5.

gandiva.name: Gandiva
gandiva.unidentified_name: a great bow that hums with stored energy
gandiva.lore: Arjuna's divine bow had one hundred strings; when one broke another appeared. Its twang shook the earth. With it Arjuna killed 100,000 soldiers in the Kurukshetra War. When grief made him hesitate before battle, Krishna delivered an 18-chapter philosophical treatise to persuade him to pick it up again.

fail_not.name: Fail-not
fail_not.unidentified_name: a yew bow with a single carved inscription
fail_not.lore: Tristan's bow, given by the fairy Morgain. Its name was its promise. The inscription reads 'Fail not.' Arrows loosed in duty flew true; arrows loosed in anger missed. Its owner learned this the hard way.
fail_not._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=57, base=16 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(57) x 1.65), min_level=45, quiz_tier=3.

kusanagi.name: Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi
kusanagi.unidentified_name: a slim blade with the scent of rain
kusanagi.lore: Found inside the eight-headed serpent Yamata no Orochi. Yamato Takeru used it to cut the grass and redirect the wind when surrounded by enemies who had set fire to the plain around him. The sword has been at the Atsuta Shrine for fourteen centuries. No one has seen it.
kusanagi._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=83, base=32 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(83) x 1.7), min_level=71, quiz_tier=5.

zulfiqar.name: Zulfiqar
zulfiqar.unidentified_name: a blade forked at the tip like a serpent's tongue
zulfiqar.lore: Given to Ali ibn Abi Talib at the Battle of Badr. 'There is no sword but Zulfiqar, and no hero but Ali.' The bifurcated tip could take two lives with one thrust. Shia tradition holds it will be wielded by the Mahdi at the end of time.

harpe.name: Harpe
harpe.unidentified_name: a curved blade with a small hooked back-edge
harpe.lore: Given to Perseus by Hermes to slay Medusa. Forged with an adamantine edge. Perseus used it while looking at Medusa's reflection in his shield. Some myths say Cronus used its predecessor to castrate Uranus. The weapon has a history of separating very important things.

trident_of_poseidon.name: Trident of Poseidon
trident_of_poseidon.unidentified_name: a three-pronged weapon of sea-dark metal
trident_of_poseidon.lore: Poseidon struck the Acropolis and produced a saltwater spring. Athena planted an olive tree. He lost the vote and flooded the Attic plain. The trident-mark is still visible on the Erechtheion floor. He used it to attempt to drown Odysseus for an entire decade.
trident_of_poseidon._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=85, base=34 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(85) x 1.7), min_level=73, quiz_tier=5.

carnwennan.name: Carnwennan
carnwennan.unidentified_name: a small white-handled knife with no visible edge
carnwennan.lore: Arthur's dagger that could shroud its wielder in shadow. Arthur used it to kill the Very Black Witch in the Valley of Grief after Kei and Bedivere had both tried and failed. The Mabinogion records this without elaboration.
carnwennan._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=34, base=8 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(34) x 1.7), min_level=26, quiz_tier=2.

mistilteinn.name: Mistilteinn
mistilteinn.unidentified_name: a blade that seems to cut shadows as well as flesh
mistilteinn.lore: The Mistletoe Sword. Mistletoe was the one substance Baldur was not protected against — his mother considered it too small to matter. The sword shares this property. Wielded by Prainn the draugr-king before Hervor took it from his barrow.
mistilteinn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=91, base=39 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(91) x 1.7), min_level=85, quiz_tier=5.

curtana.name: Curtana
curtana.unidentified_name: a broad two-handed blade with a blunt squared tip
curtana.lore: The Sword of Mercy — its tip broken by an angel at the moment Ogier the Dane was about to kill Charlemagne's son. The broken tip became the symbol of mercy in justice. English coronation regalia still includes a blunt-tipped Sword of Mercy. Mercy is the lesser blade.

parashu.name: Parashu
parashu.unidentified_name: a divine axe of celestial bronze
parashu.lore: Shiva gave Parashu to Parashurama after ten thousand years of penance. Parashurama used it to exterminate the Kshatriya caste twenty-one times over, filling five lakes with blood. He is considered a great teacher of martial arts.

labrys.name: Labrys
labrys.lore: The double-headed axe of Minoan Crete — labrys means both the axe and the labyrinth. It appears in every Minoan palace fresco, held by women. Modern scholars believe it was primarily religious. The Minotaur had no sword, only size, darkness, and the certainty that no one wanted to be there.
labrys._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=24, base=6 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(24) x 1.65), min_level=16, quiz_tier=2.

chandrahas.name: Chandrahas
chandrahas.unidentified_name: a curved blade cold as moonlight
chandrahas.lore: Shiva gave the Moon's Laughter to Ravana after Ravana lifted Mount Kailash with twenty arms. Shiva added the condition that if used for evil it would return to him. Ravana used it for evil almost immediately. The sword returned. This is the problem with giving extraordinary weapons as gifts.

laevateinn.name: Laevateinn
laevateinn.unidentified_name: a staff cut from the world-tree with a notch at the top
laevateinn.lore: Loki cut it at the gates of Hel. It can destroy Vidofnir, the golden rooster atop Yggdrasil whose crowing will begin Ragnarok. Sinmara guards it and will only surrender it through a series of impossible trades. Preventing Ragnarok is bureaucratically complicated.
laevateinn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=93, base=40 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(93) x 1.7), min_level=87, quiz_tier=5.

thyrsus.name: Thyrsus of Dionysus
thyrsus.unidentified_name: a giant fennel stalk topped with a pine cone
thyrsus.lore: The Maenads carried the thyrsus. In the Bacchae, Agave kills her son Pentheus with it, believing in her madness he is a lion. Dionysus watched. This is the instrument of a god who believed experience was the teacher.
thyrsus._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=32, base=7 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(32) x 1.5), min_level=24, quiz_tier=2.

rod_of_moses.name: Rod of Moses
rod_of_moses.unidentified_name: a plain shepherd's crook of ancient wood
rod_of_moses.lore: The rod became a serpent in Pharaoh's court; parted the Red Sea; struck the rock at Horeb. Jewish tradition gives it a provenance from Adam through Noah through Abraham. Moses used it. Aaron used it. No one is certain what happened to it afterward.
rod_of_moses._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=84, base=31 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(84) x 1.65), min_level=72, quiz_tier=5.

amenonuhoko.name: Amenonuhoko
amenonuhoko.unidentified_name: a jeweled spear dripping with brine
amenonuhoko.lore: The Heavenly Jeweled Spear, given to Izanagi and Izanami by the elder gods. They stirred the primordial ocean with it and from the brine that dripped from its tip, the first island of Japan was born. Each kill sends a ripple of primordial stillness through nearby enemies.

sudarshana.name: Sudarshana Chakra
sudarshana.unidentified_name: a spinning disc of burning light
sudarshana.lore: Vishnu's spinning discus. Forged from the effulgence of the sun itself. When Shiva asked to test Vishnu's most powerful weapon, Vishnu threw it without warning and cut off one of Shiva's heads. Shiva grew a new one. They considered this a satisfactory test.
sudarshana._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=93, base=39 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(93) x 1.65).

ridill.name: Ridill
ridill.unidentified_name: a short blade from the dwarf-hoard
ridill.lore: One of two swords in Fafnir's hoard alongside Gram. Sigurd left it when he took Gram. Ridill was the shorter blade — a dwarf-forged knife of theoretical powers, present at every great event of the Volsung cycle, never called upon. Its potential remains forever theoretical.
ridill._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=55, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(55) x 1.5), min_level=43, quiz_tier=3.

kladenets.name: Samosek
kladenets.unidentified_name: a blade that seems to move before you do
kladenets.lore: The Self-Swinger of Slavic fairy tales fights on its own. It is found in underground kingdoms guarded by Koschei or a serpent. Heroes who find it never quite understand it. The sword fights; they survive. The sword's autonomy is treated not as alarming but as practical.
kladenets._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=58, base=17 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(58) x 1.7), min_level=46, quiz_tier=3.

shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.name: Shamshir-e Zomorrodnegar
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.unidentified_name: an emerald-inlaid curved blade of Solomonic make
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.lore: The Emerald-Studded Sword of Solomon could bind and command djinn. On each emerald a name of power was engraved. Solomon used it not as a weapon but as an administrative tool, employing djinn in constructing the Temple. Its use as a management instrument is rarely discussed in Western traditions.

chrysaor.name: Chrysaor
chrysaor.unidentified_name: a golden-bladed sword of divine origin
chrysaor.lore: Chrysaor — the Golden Sword — sprang from Medusa's neck alongside Pegasus when Perseus beheaded her. He carried it through his life and gave it to his son Geryones, who built a kingdom in the far west with its aid. Heracles killed Geryones and the sword passed from the western world's records. Gold swords appear occasionally in Bronze Age hoards. None have been identified as Chrysaor. None have been ruled out.

caliburn.name: Caliburn
caliburn.unidentified_name: a plain but perfectly balanced blade
caliburn.lore: Some scholars distinguish Caliburn — the sword in the stone — from Excalibur, the sword from the lake. Geoffrey of Monmouth uses the name Caliburnus and has it forged in Avalon. In later tradition it became a single weapon. The distinction matters because the stone-sword test and the lake-gift are morally opposite stories: one is earned, one is given. Arthur had both.
caliburn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=37, base=10 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(37) x 1.7), min_level=29, quiz_tier=2.

brisingr.name: Brisingr
brisingr.unidentified_name: a blade that runs warm to the touch
brisingr.lore: The word for fire in Old Norse. A sword that shares its name with the ancient word for flame was found in a Norse burial mound in Gotland, its blade still faintly warm centuries later. The metallurgists who examined it in 1947 published their findings in a paper that was subsequently lost. Three colleagues confirmed its content before it vanished. The sword itself remains in a private collection.

fragarach_the_whisperer.name: Whisperer
fragarach_the_whisperer.unidentified_name: a dagger that makes almost no sound
fragarach_the_whisperer.lore: A blade said to have been forged by the same smith who made Fragarach, intended as its companion. Where Fragarach answered questions loudly, this blade worked silently. Assassins across four centuries reported finding it rather than seeking it. It was present at the deaths of seven significant historical figures. Twice it was present at the survival of one.
fragarach_the_whisperer._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=38, base=9 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(38) x 1.55), min_level=30, quiz_tier=2.

naegling.name: Naegling
naegling.unidentified_name: a heavy single-bladed axe with an age-worn grip
naegling.lore: Beowulf's sword that shattered in his final battle with the dragon. The poem notes that iron could not help him — his grip was too strong for ordinary blades. Naegling broke. He had to kill the dragon with his bare hands and a knife. This is what happens when a warrior outlives the weapons made for lesser men.
naegling._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=54, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(54) x 1.55), min_level=42, quiz_tier=3.

punch_in_the_face.name: Punch in the Face
punch_in_the_face.lore: This is Dad’s fist. It is legendary. It has never missed. It has never needed to miss twice. Scientists have attempted to measure the force behind it and their instruments simply stopped working out of respect.

hunt_captains_sword.name: Hunt Captain's Sword
hunt_captains_sword.lore: Taken from the captain of the Wild Hunt, this blade phases between this world and the spectral realm. Its edge is impossibly sharp and its cold is the cold of the grave.

wendigo_fang.name: Wendigo's Fang
wendigo_fang.lore: A fang torn from the Wendigo's maw. It leaches warmth and stamina from enemies on contact. The wound never feels warm again.

echidna_fang.name: Echidna's Fang
echidna_fang.lore: A tooth from Echidna herself, mother of all monsters. Wounds from it fester with a slow-acting venom that mimics her many children's poisons.

vulcans_brand.name: Vulcan's Brand
vulcans_brand.lore: Forged in Vulcan's own furnace by Cacus who stole the technique from his father. The blade never fully cools and sets enemies alight on a solid strike.

sling_of_david.name: Sling of David
sling_of_david.unidentified_name: a worn leather strap with a pouch
sling_of_david.lore: The shepherd boy David faced the giant Goliath with nothing but a sling and five smooth stones. One stone was enough. The sling is the weapon of the underestimated — it asks only for courage and accuracy. Against the mighty, it is devastating.

prometheus_torch.name: Narthex of Prometheus
prometheus_torch.lore: Hesiod's Theogony says Prometheus stole fire in a hollow fennel stalk — a narthex, the dry pithy stem that smolders slowly inside without burning through. He carried Zeus's ember down to mortals that way. Zeus chained him to the Caucasus and sent an eagle for his liver every day. The stalk in your hand still smokes at the core. It has not gone out for three thousand years.

sword_of_damocles.name: Sword of Damocles
sword_of_damocles.unidentified_name: a jeweled blade suspended by a single horsehair
sword_of_damocles.lore: Dionysius II of Syracuse invited the courtier Damocles to sit on his throne and enjoy the luxuries of power. Above the throne hung a sword, suspended by a single horsehair. Damocles understood immediately: power comes with constant peril. This blade cuts magnificently, but the thread grows thinner with every swing.

robin_hoods_longbow.name: Robin Hood's Longbow
robin_hoods_longbow.unidentified_name: a weathered yew longbow wrapped in green cloth
robin_hoods_longbow.lore: Robin of Loxley, the outlaw of Sherwood Forest, could split an arrow at two hundred paces. His longbow was cut from a yew tree in the heart of the forest. It favors those who strike from the shadows — enemies that cannot see you cannot hear its string.

achilles_spear.name: Achilles's Spear
achilles_spear.unidentified_name: a bronze-tipped ash spear with a worn grip
achilles_spear.lore: The spear of Achilles, son of Peleus, forged by Hephaestus. In the myth of Telephus, the spear that wounded also healed — rust scraped from its tip cured the very wound it had made. Those slain by this spear restore vigor to their killer. At Troy, no warrior could stand before it.

gilgamesh_axe.name: Gilgamesh's Axe
gilgamesh_axe.unidentified_name: a heavy bronze axe with cuneiform inscriptions
gilgamesh_axe.lore: Enkidu dreamed of an axe that fell from the sky — Gilgamesh's equal, his brother in arms. This is that axe: the weapon of the king who sought immortality and found friendship instead. In the Cedar Forest, Gilgamesh and Enkidu fought Humbaba together. The axe remembers that bond — it strikes harder after its wielder has been wounded.

cronus_scythe.name: Cronus's Scythe
cronus_scythe.unidentified_name: a curved blade that distorts the air around it
cronus_scythe.lore: Gaia gave this adamantine scythe to Cronus to overthrow his father Uranus. With it, Cronus castrated the sky itself — from the blood sprang the Giants and the Furies, and from the severed flesh arose Aphrodite. The scythe cuts through time and matter alike. Those it wounds age visibly, their vitality draining with each passing moment.

spear_of_lugh.name: Spear of Lugh
spear_of_lugh.lore: One of the Four Treasures of the Tuatha De Danann. The Spear of Lugh was so bloodthirsty it had to be kept submerged in a cauldron of poison to prevent it from igniting everything nearby. No battle was ever sustained against it. Lugh used it to slay Balor of the Evil Eye at the Second Battle of Mag Tuired, striking through his eye and out the back of his head.

gae_dearg.name: Gae Dearg
gae_dearg.unidentified_name: a crimson-stained spear that weeps red
gae_dearg.lore: The Red Spear of Diarmuid Ua Duibhne, champion of the Fianna. Diarmuid carried two spears: Gae Buidhe the Yellow, which wounded but could not kill, and Gae Dearg the Red, from which no wound could ever heal. The distinction mattered — Diarmuid chose his spear based on whether mercy was warranted. Gae Dearg offers no mercy.

net_of_hephaestus.name: Net of Hephaestus
net_of_hephaestus.lore: Hephaestus forged this net to catch Ares and Aphrodite in their affair. It was so fine it was invisible, so strong not even Ares could break free. In the Odyssey, Demodocus sings of how Hephaestus dragged the ensnared lovers before all the gods of Olympus. This net does almost no damage — but nothing escapes it.

sword_of_michael.name: Sword of Michael
sword_of_michael.unidentified_name: a blade of blinding white radiance
sword_of_michael.lore: The flaming sword of the Archangel Michael, Prince of the Heavenly Host. With this blade he cast Lucifer from Heaven and shall wield it again at the end of days. No armor, no enchantment, no infernal resistance can turn its edge. Against the Destroyer, it blazes with the full wrath of Heaven. It is the reward of the righteous — earned not by strength but by the quality of one's soul.

oathkeeper_sword.name: Oathkeeper
oathkeeper_sword.lore: A longsword of excellent make, the name VALE engraved into the crossguard. It was carried into the dungeon by a young man who wanted to prove himself. He didn't come back. The blade is still sharp — someone maintained it with love.

penitents_blade.name: Penitent's Blade
penitents_blade.unidentified_name: a dark iron dagger stained with old blood
penitents_blade.lore: A wickedly sharp dagger of dark iron, carried for twenty years by a man who used it to kill. The blade drinks blood — wounds dealt with it restore the wielder's vitality, as though the weapon is trying to balance its ledger.

boomstick.name: Boomstick
boomstick.lore: This is my BOOMSTICK! It's a twelve-gauge double-barreled Remington. S-Mart's top of the line. You can find this in the sporting goods department. That's right, this sweet baby was made in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Retails for about $109.95. It's got a walnut stock, cobalt blue steel, and a hair trigger. That's right. Shop smart. Shop S-Mart.

chainsaw_prosthetic.name: Chainsaw Prosthetic
chainsaw_prosthetic.unidentified_name: a chainsaw bolted to an arm stump
chainsaw_prosthetic.lore: A Homelite XL chainsaw, permanently bolted to the stump of a severed right hand. The original owner attached it in a moment of desperate improvisation in a remote cabin in Tennessee. It has since carved through more deadites than anyone cares to count. Groovy.

romulus_spear.name: Spear of Romulus
romulus_spear.unidentified_name: a bronze-tipped spear with wolf-hide grip
romulus_spear.lore: When Romulus hurled his spear from the Aventine Hill into the Palatine, it struck the earth and took root, growing into a great tree. The spear that founded Rome carries the will of a man who built a civilization from nothing — from fratricide to empire. It strikes from further than any common weapon.

pharaohs_crook.name: Pharaoh's Crook
pharaohs_crook.lore: The crook and flail were the symbols of pharaonic authority in ancient Egypt — the crook representing the shepherd's duty to guide and protect, the flail representing the power to punish. This crook once rested in the crossed arms of a king. Its strikes carry the weight of divine kingship, stunning those who would oppose the throne.

mjolnir_shard.name: Mjolnir Shard
mjolnir_shard.unidentified_name: a heavy iron fragment crackling with static
mjolnir_shard.lore: A jagged fragment of Thor's legendary hammer, Mjolnir — the weapon forged by the dwarves Sindri and Brokkr in Asgard. Though only a shard, it still carries the storm. Lightning arcs between its fractures, and each blow echoes with distant thunder. To wield even a piece of Mjolnir is to hold a fraction of the storm god's wrath.

bow_of_rama.name: Bow of Rama
bow_of_rama.unidentified_name: a recurved bow radiating faint heat
bow_of_rama.lore: The great bow of Lord Rama, hero of the Ramayana — the divine prince who bent the bow of Shiva to win Sita's hand. His arrows, guided by dharma, struck down the demon king Ravana and his armies. This bow carries that sacred fire. Arrows loosed from it burn with righteous flame, and no act of evil can stand before it.

gae_bolg_fragment.name: Gae Bolg Fragment
gae_bolg_fragment.unidentified_name: a barbed bone spearhead bound to a shaft
gae_bolg_fragment.lore: A fragment of the Gae Bolg, the cursed spear of Cu Chulainn, greatest hero of Irish mythology. The original weapon was made from the bone of a sea monster and, once it pierced flesh, its barbs opened inside the wound, making it impossible to remove without killing the victim. Even this fragment carries that terrible legacy — its strikes rend deep, and its critical blows are devastating.

staff_of_moses.name: Staff of Moses
staff_of_moses.unidentified_name: a weathered staff of ancient wood
staff_of_moses.lore: The staff that Moses raised to part the Red Sea, that struck the rock at Horeb to bring forth water, that became a serpent before Pharaoh. It was a simple shepherd's staff before God chose it — and that is the lesson. It is not the weapon that matters, but the hand that wields it and the faith behind it. Against the unholy, it strikes with divine authority.

witcher_silver_blade.name: Witcher's Silver Blade
witcher_silver_blade.unidentified_name: a blade of polished silver etched with runes
witcher_silver_blade.lore: A witcher's silver sword, forged for one purpose: killing monsters. Where steel is for men, silver is for creatures of the night — wraiths, vampires, ghouls, and the nameless things that crawl from cursed earth. This blade was carried through a hundred contracts by a white-haired witcher who was more than human but never quite monster. The runes along its edge hum faintly in the presence of dark magic.

zireael.name: Zireael
zireael.unidentified_name: an impossibly light sword with a swallow engraved on the blade
zireael.lore: Zireael — 'Swallow' in Elder Speech. Forged by the gnome swordsmith Esterhazy of Mahakam, this blade is a masterwork of metallurgy and magic. Lighter than any human-forged sword yet harder than dwarven steel, it was made for a girl who carried the blood of the Elder Folk in her veins. The swallow engraved on the ricasso is not merely decorative — it is a promise. She will return. She always returns.

vel_of_murugan.name: Vel of Murugan
vel_of_murugan.unidentified_name: a bronze lance that radiates heat
vel_of_murugan.lore: The Vel was given to Murugan by his mother Parvati to slay the demon Surapadman. When thrown, it split the demon in two — one half became a peacock, the other a rooster. The lance returned to Murugan's hand. It burns with the fire of righteous war and cannot be turned aside by mortal shields.

khopesh_of_anubis.name: Khopesh of Anubis
khopesh_of_anubis.unidentified_name: a curved sickle-blade of black iron
khopesh_of_anubis.lore: Anubis weighed the heart of every Egyptian dead against the feather of Ma'at, truth itself. If the heart was heavier, the demon Ammit ate it on the spot. The priests of Anubis carried khopeshes of black iron during the embalming rites — not for use on the living, but for the symbolic severing of what could not be allowed into the next world. This is one of them. The blade still measures, and what it judges, it keeps.

chandrahasa.name: Chandrahasa
chandrahasa.unidentified_name: a crescent-shaped blade that glows faintly
chandrahasa.lore: The 'Laughing Moon,' given to Ravana by Shiva himself as a reward for his devotion. The blade laughed as it cut — a high, cold sound like cracking ice. It grows more dangerous as its wielder's life fades, channeling desperation into devastating power. Shiva warned Ravana never to use it unjustly, or it would return to him. Ravana did not listen.

green_chapel_axe.name: Green Chapel Axe
green_chapel_axe.unidentified_name: a green-hafted axe with living vines
green_chapel_axe.lore: The axe carried by the Green Knight into Arthur's hall on New Year's Day. He offered a game: any knight may strike one blow, if the Green Knight may return it in a year. Gawain took the challenge and cut off the Knight's head. The Knight picked it up and left. The axe remembers. When its wielder is struck, the wound begins to close — slowly, but surely.

aiglos.name: Aiglos
aiglos.lore: Snow-point, the spear of Gil-galad the last High King of the Noldor, who fell at the Last Alliance before the gates of Barad-dur. He hewed at the Dark Lord himself with this and was burned to ash by the contact. The spear endured. It does not lose its edge and it does not warm in the hand.

akinakes_acrisius.name: Akinakes of Acrisius
akinakes_acrisius.lore: The short, leaf-shaped blade of Acrisius, king of Argos, who locked his daughter Danae in a bronze tower because an oracle said her son would kill him. Perseus killed him anyway, by accident, with a discus throw at funeral games. The blade survived the prophecy. The blades always do.

anduril.name: Anduril
anduril.lore: Flame of the West, reforged from the shards of Narsil by the smiths of Imladris. The blade that cut the Ring from Sauron's hand, broken when Isildur fell, sleeping for an Age in Rivendell until the Heir of Elendil came to claim it. The Dead of Dunharrow followed it down the Paths and a city held the line.

atalanta_bow.name: Atalanta's Bow
atalanta_bow.lore: The huntress raised by bears, fastest of mortals, who drew first blood on the Calydonian Boar before any of the heroes could land a spear. Meleager awarded her the hide, and his uncles died for the slight. Her arrow flies straight to the first thing that draws breath in her sights.

bellerophon_lance.name: Bellerophon's Lance
bellerophon_lance.lore: Tipped with a lump of lead, this is the lance Bellerophon couched from the back of Pegasus when he charged the Chimera. The monster's own fire melted the lead in its throat, and the molten metal did the killing the spearhead alone could not. Pride later threw Bellerophon off the winged horse; the lance survived him.

cadmus_sword.name: Sword of Cadmus
cadmus_sword.lore: Cadmus of Tyre slew the great water-dragon of Ares at the spring that would water Thebes. Athena told him to sow the teeth in the furrow; the Sown Men sprang up armed and killed each other until five remained to found the city. The sword that opened the dragon is the same sword that opened the founding line.

glamdring.name: Glamdring
glamdring.lore: Foe-Hammer, the orc-cleaver. Forged in Gondolin during the First Age, lost when the hidden city burned, recovered from a stone-troll's hoard in the wilderlands. Gandalf carried it through Moria and into the deep where the Balrog waited. The blade glows blue when goblins are near, which is most of the time, this far down.

hector_javelin.name: Hector's Javelin
hector_javelin.lore: The bronze-headed javelin of Hector, breaker of horses, last shield of Troy. He threw one like it at Ajax in the duel before the ships; it struck the boss of the shield and bent. Patroclus wore Achilles's armor when he fell to the next throw of its kind.

heracles_club.name: Heracles's Olive-Club
heracles_club.lore: Uprooted from the wild olives of Nemea by the hero's own hands, hardened in the fire of his second labor. The Nemean Lion's hide had turned every blade he tried; the club did not need to cut. The wood is dark with old work and smells of resin even now.

hofud.name: Hofud
hofud.lore: Hofud, called Man-Head, the sword of Heimdall the watcher at Bifrost. He hears wool growing on the backs of sheep and grass climbing out of the ground. At Ragnarok he and Loki will meet on the field and finish each other; the sword will not survive that day either, but until then nothing slips past it.

meleager_spear.name: Meleager's Boar-Spear
meleager_spear.lore: The ash-shafted spear with which Meleager pinned the Calydonian Boar that Artemis sent in vengeance for a forgotten sacrifice. His mother carried a brand from his birth-fire; when he killed her brothers over Atalanta's prize, she threw it on the hearth, and the hero burned with it. The spear was a king's weapon either way.

pelops_sword.name: Sword of Pelops
pelops_sword.lore: Pelops took the kingdom of Pisa by winning the chariot race against Oenomaus, after bribing the charioteer to remove a linchpin. The king died. The charioteer was thrown into the sea cursing the house. The sword passed down to Atreus, then to Agamemnon, and Mycenae did not stop bleeding for three generations.

stormbringer.name: Stormbringer
stormbringer.lore: Black runesword, forged by the Lords of Chaos at the dawn of the Young Kingdoms. It drinks souls and feeds them to its bearer; Elric of Melnibone leaned on it for his strength and lost everyone he loved to its hunger. At the end of the world the blade laughed and named itself a god. It will turn in the hand if the chance is right.

talos_sickle.name: Sickle of Talos
talos_sickle.lore: A curved bronze blade said to be ground from one of the molten drops shed when Medea pulled the brass pin from Talos's ankle. The Cretan giant bled his ichor into the sea before he fell. Whatever cooled there still cuts.

theseus_club.name: Theseus's Club
theseus_club.lore: The bronze club Theseus took from the corpse of Periphetes, the lame brigand of Epidaurus who beat travellers to death with it. Theseus kept the weapon for the rest of the road to Athens and carried it down into the labyrinth. The hero who walked the maze did not walk it empty-handed.

cain_club.name: Cain's Club
cain_club.unidentified_name: a crude root-end cudgel stained at the head
cain_club.lore: The Bible does not say what Cain used. Talmudic and Quranic commentary settles on a rough club — the first murder weapon, made of nothing in particular. The mark on Cain protected him from retaliation but not from memory. The wood is the wrong colour at one end and no one has been able to wash it clean.

wepwawet_mace.name: Mace of Wepwawet
wepwawet_mace.unidentified_name: a slender ceremonial mace topped with a jackal
wepwawet_mace.lore: Wepwawet — 'Opener of the Ways' — was the jackal-headed war-god of Upper Egypt, older than Anubis and originally separate from him. The Pyramid Texts show him going before the king as scout and standard-bearer, his iconography listing both a mace and a bow. Predynastic pear-shaped mace heads from Hierakonpolis survive in museum cases. They are heavier than they look, and the carved limestone ones are heaviest of all.

cuchulainn_hurley.name: Setanta's Hurley
cuchulainn_hurley.unidentified_name: a worn ash hurling stick with a stone-hard heel
cuchulainn_hurley.lore: Before he was Cu Chulainn — Culann's Hound — he was Setanta, the boy who killed Culann's guard dog by driving a hurling ball down its throat with this stick. He volunteered to replace the dog. The name stuck. The hurley is ash and the heel is dense as river stone.

mwindo_axe.name: Mwindo's Conga-Scepter
mwindo_axe.unidentified_name: a small carved axe-scepter inlaid with cowrie shells
mwindo_axe.lore: The Mwindo Epic — collected from the Banyanga of the eastern Congo in the 1950s — gives its hero a conga-scepter that did the work of an axe, a magic wand, and a flyswatter. Born speaking, born walking, born with this in his hand. He used it to bring his uncles back from the dead, and once to kill a dragon.
